candidates.exact_span: effluent limitations for total suspended solids (TSS) at monthly average of 20 mg/l and daily maximum of 30 mg/l
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes the enforceable numeric TSS limits (monthly average and daily maximum) against which reported measurements would be compared; different readings of which parameters or limit types apply would change limit-selection and exceedance determinations.

candidates.exact_span: using BPJ, effluent limitations for TSS are established in the draft permit identical to the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Links current TSS limits to BPJ derivation and prior-permit continuity; interpreting whether limits are newly established, carried forward unchanged, or contingent on similarity to other facilities could change which numeric limits are treated as operative for FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Loading limits are not established since the discharge is not a continuous one and is discharged from a holding lagoon on an as needed basis.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Explicitly excludes loading limits from applicability while characterizing discharge as intermittent and lagoon-based; different interpretations of 'not established,' 'not continuous,' or 'as needed' could change which numeric limits apply (A), when monitoring is required (B), and how no-discharge or conditional periods are classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: monthly average of 20 mg/l and daily maximum of 30 mg/l
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies averaging period and maximum type for TSS compliance; interpretation of required sampling frequency, averaging windows, and event coverage needed to demonstrate monthly average versus daily maximum compliance could change which monitoring obligations are deemed applicable.

candidates.exact_span: the low (0.177 MGD) volume of discharges
candidates.computation_change_reason: States a specific discharge-flow magnitude used in dilution and downstream-effects reasoning; different acceptance of this volume figure could affect whether dilution-based arguments support additional or fewer water-quality-based limits (A) and how periods of low or no discharge are documented versus unresolved (C).

candidates.exact_span: the water quality standards of the Navajo Nation will not be affected
candidates.computation_change_reason: Asserts that downstream tribal WQS are not implicated; interpreting this as a basis for omitting more stringent water-quality-based effluent limits versus merely descriptive rationale could change whether enforceable numeric limits beyond the stated TSS values are treated as applicable.

candidates.exact_span: Where these technology-based permit limits do not protect water quality or the designated uses, additional water quality-based effluent limitations and/or conditions are included in the NPDES permits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets the trigger for imposing water-quality-based effluent limits beyond technology-based controls; different readings of whether protection is adequate for this discharge could change which numeric limits are considered enforceable for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: General criteria are applicable as specified in 20.6.4.13 NMAC.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies which state general water-quality criteria apply to the discharge; interpretation of applicability under 20.6.4.13 NMAC could change whether narrative or derived numeric water-quality-based limits supplement the stated TSS limits.

candidates.exact_span: The discharge from the facility may enter Lower Animas Ditch / Hampton Arroyo and/or Williams Arroyo in Water body
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies uncertain receiving-water routing ('may enter' and 'and/or'); different resolution of which water body receives the discharge could change which state water-quality standards and associated effluent limits are treated as applicable.
